name: Employment lawsuits per $bn revenue
description: Federal employment-discrimination, wage and labor lawsuits filed against the company per $bn revenue - direct evidence of how it treats employees. Caveats: it only captures disputes reaching federal court, so firms with mandatory arbitration score better; subsidiaries under different names are undercounted.

name: Corporate PAC money per $M revenue
description: Dollars the company's own federal PAC contributes to candidates and political committees per $M of revenue - money spent buying access to legislators rather than creating impact. Caveat: it only sees the company's own FEC-registered PAC, so lobbying fees, trade-association dues, 527s and dark money are invisible, and the 190 companies with no PAC all tie at zero.

name: Shareholder payout ratio (buybacks + dividends / operating cash flow)
description: Share buybacks plus dividends paid as a share of net operating cash flow - it measures how much of the cash a business generates is extracted for shareholders rather than reinvested in the workforce, wages, training and capability, the standard financialisation critique and the shareholder-versus-stakeholder balance that frameworks such as JUST Capital treat as a core stakeholder dimension; a company with no buybacks and no dividends is a real 0, while company-years with non-positive operating cash flow or a ratio above 10x are omitted rather than clipped because the denominator, not the payout, would drive the number.

name: CEO-to-median-worker pay ratio
description: CEO total compensation as a multiple of the median employee's, as every US-listed company must disclose in its proxy (SEC Item 402(u)) - a lower ratio means the company's rewards are shared more fairly with its workers.

name: Employer retirement contribution per participant
description: Employer contributions to the company's US 401(k)-type plans per active participant (Form 5500 Schedule H) - more means the employer funds more of its workers' retirement security. Caveat: US plans only, defined-benefit pensions excluded.

name: Workplace injury and illness rate (TRIR)
description: Recordable work injuries and illnesses per 100 full-time workers at the company's US establishments (OSHA Form 300A) - a lower rate means fewer people get hurt at work. Caveat: industries exempt from OSHA record keeping (banks, software, real estate) have no data.

name: Human capital disclosure specificity
description: How many of eight quantified workforce disclosure types (headcount, gender or ethnic representation %, turnover/retention rate, training hours or spend, a safety rate, a pay-equity figure, an engagement score, union coverage) the company actually puts numbers on in the Human Capital Resources section of its most recent 10-K, which every filer must write since 2020 - measuring whether a company counts its workforce or only writes about it. Main weakness: it measures disclosure quality, NOT workforce outcomes - a company can disclose beautifully and still treat its people badly.
